title: FSDP2 Unwrap model, still has dtensors as weights
author: kiansierra

comments.author: kiansierra
comments.body:
The below seems to be a hack, to manage to save to safetensors.

```py
...
trainer.train()
from torch.distributed.tensor import DTensor

state_dict = model.state_dict()
for key, value in state_dict.items():
    if isinstance(value, DTensor):
        state_dict[key] = value.to_local()
accelerator.wait_for_everyone()
model.save_pretrained(training_args.output_dir, state_dict=state_dict)
```

comments.author: S1ro1
comments.body: @kiansierra This is still a WIP, for now you can use `accelerator.save_state` to save the model. I'll update you when I fix this, it's related to `FSDP2` not having full state dict, but having to implement it ourselves.

comments.author: Craigacp
comments.body:
> The below seems to be a hack, to manage to save to safetensors.
> 
> ```python
> trainer.train()
> from torch.distributed.tensor import DTensor
> 
> state_dict = model.state_dict()
> for key, value in state_dict.items():
>     if isinstance(value, DTensor):
>         state_dict[key] = value.to_local()
> accelerator.wait_for_everyone()
> model.save_pretrained(training_args.output_dir, state_dict=state_dict)
>```

This doesn't work as `value.to_local()` gives you the local shard not the full tensor. Using `value.full_tensor()` gives the full state dict back, but then if it's too big to fit on the GPU there are issues. Not sure if there's a way to offload only a single copy of the state dict to the CPU, I can see how to dump 1 per GPU, but I'd rather not materialize 280GB * 8 copies if it can be avoided.

comments.author: S1ro1
comments.body:
This is very much in WIP, but there's a PR to support DTensors in `save_pretrained` which I'm pretty sure minimises the memory usage as much as possible: https://github.com/huggingface/transformers/pull/37919

It relies on another pr in Huggingface_hub but we're working on getting it as effective as possible @Craigacp 

Also you can use `torch.distributed.checkpoint.get_state_dict` as here: https://github.com/huggingface/accelerate/commit/8fb073536a1e1607d7fb6262051e5712c8cec705 to get it, though I was getting some issues with it

comments.author: Craigacp
comments.body:
Yeah,`get_state_dict` wasn't working for me either, I was hitting the invalid storage error. I've got a workaround to not materialize it `n` times on the CPU which I'm currently testing out.

Fixing `save_pretrained` to work with DTensors will be nice, I'll keep an eye out for when that lands.

comments.author: Craigacp
comments.body:
This works for me:
```python
from torch.distributed.checkpoint.state_dict import get_state_dict

state_dict, _ = get_state_dict(model, [])
# Coalesce the full state dict
for key, value in state_dict.items():
    if isinstance(value, DTensor):
        # materialize full tensor on each GPU
        local_full_value = value.full_tensor()
    else:
        local_full_value = value
    if accelerator.process_index == 0:
        # to avoid materializing the full model on CPU once per GPU we discard it if we're not the main process
        state_dict[key] = local_full_value.cpu()
accelerator.wait_for_everyone()
if accelerator.process_index == 0:
    model.save_pretrained(output_dir, state_dict, is_main_process=True)
accelerator.wait_for_everyone()
```

comments.author: S1ro1
comments.body: You can use options as described [here](https://pytorch.org/docs/stable/distributed.checkpoint.html#torch.distributed.checkpoint.state_dict.StateDictOptions) to do this torch native way, it is gonna be upstreamed to `accelerate` in `get_state_dict` when I figure out why it sometimes hangs when using cpu_offload=True.

comments.author: Craigacp
comments.body: Yeah, I need CPU offloading to work consistently, so when that bug gets figured out I'll go back to using the options as for the time being the code I posted is behaving itself.
